title: Hiring pulse sprint and interviewer feedback loop
summary: A compact, repeatable 3-week hiring sprint process with an embedded interviewer feedback loop and a lightweight day0-21 onboarding checklist to reduce time-to-ramp and interviewer variance.
content: Context: We need a repeatable sprints-based hiring cadence for small IC+manager roles to reduce cycle time while improving interview quality. This doc collates a hiring sprint plan, an interviewer rubric (practical, behavior+skill), and a short operational onboarding checklist for the first 21 days.
Objectives:
- Shorten open-to-offer time for priority roles from 45 -> 21 days for sprints where candidate flow is healthy.
- Improve calibration across interviewers via a structured immediate feedback loop after each interview batch.
- Ensure new hires hit basic platform orientation and first-ship milestones in 21 days.
When to use this pattern:
- Role scope is well-defined and hiring priority is high (e.g., capacity to ramp a pod).
- Hiring manager and PEOPLE-OPS commit to a 3-week sprint cadence with weekly checkpoints.
- Minimum interview panel (sourcing, hiring manager, 2 tech interviewers, culture fit).
Sprint overview (21-day cadence):
Week 0 - Sprint prep (3 days):
- Align on role outcomes & success metrics (Engineer: first PR to infra repo, PM: first roadmap slot defined).
- Finalize scorecard and posting copy; approve compensation band.
- Schedule interview blocks and reserve panel slots in calendars.
Week 1 - Sourcing + Screen (7 days):
- Day 1-3: Active sourcing (inbound, outreach), 1st-screen by recruiter (30m).
- Day 4-7: Shortlist 6-10 candidates to full interview loop; share candidate one-pagers with panel.
Week 2 - Interviewing + Feedback (7 days):
- Conduct full loops in two 3-hour blocks (AM/PM) on two days.
- After each block: 30-minute calibration session with panel to normalize scoring.
- Recruiter compiles consolidated feedback within 24 hours.
Week 3 - Decision + Offer + Onboard plan (4 days):
- Hiring manager makes decision within 48 hours of last interview.
- Recruiter prepares offer materials and preboarding checklist.
- If offer accepted: schedule day0 orientation and team welcome (within one week).
Interviewer feedback loop (operational flow):
1) Immediately after each interview: interviewer adds raw notes into the feedback sheet (max 10 bullet points).
2) Recruiter highlights conflicting ratings and flags areas for calibration.
3) Panel calibration meeting after each interview block to review 3-5 borderline candidates.
4) Post-hire: 30-day interviewer retrospective (what signals predicted performance vs reality).
Practical interview rubric (single-page, 1-10 scale):
- Role alignment (how clearly candidate understands role outputs) [1-10],
- Technical problem solving (structured approach + correctness) [1-10],
- System design / architecture sense (scale, tradeoffs) [1-10],
- Code craft / quality (tests, readability, refactorability) [1-10] — for engineering roles
- Product judgement / stakeholder tradeoffs — for PM roles [1-10],
- Collaboration and communication (cross-team, async) [1-10],
- Learning mindset (growth examples, post-mortem thinking) [1-10],
- Culture fit signals (values-aligned behaviors) [1-10],
- Risk flags (signals that would block hire) single-line note,
- Summary recommendation: Hire / No Hire / Maybe with conditions (mentorship plan, senior support).
Interviewer guidance (short heuristics):
- Use examples: ask for specific PRs, decisions, or metrics — avoid hypotheticals without concrete past examples.
- Score conservatively early in the week; use calibration sessions to adjust rather than re-scoring later.
- Note three concrete strengths and one principal risk per candidate. If you can’t name a principal risk, push for more probing.
Bias mitigation quick checklist for interviewers:
- Prefer behavioral anchors over impressions: ask 'tell me about a time...'
- Separate culture signals from personal background; prefer behavior evidence.
- When uncertain, compare candidate to a defined role outcome, not to an idealized person.
Operational templates (short):
- Recruiter interview summary email: one-paragraph TL;DR, 3 bullets (strengths), 1 risk, score average, next steps. Use subject: Hiring Sprint: [Role] candidate - {first last}.
- Candidate one-pager (internal): 6 lines — quick background, most recent impact, role-fit bullet, compensation note, availability, recruiter link.
Onboarding mini-checklist: Day0 -> Day21 (operational highlights):
Day 0-1 (Orientation):
- Welcome email + calendar of first 2 weeks, Slack intro in team channel, L1 access to email and dev VPN.
- 60–90 minute orientation slot: HR + benefits + security briefing + manager 1:1.
Day 2-7 (Foundations):
- Engineering: small environment setup ticket with step-by-step runbook; complete dev env and CI linting test.
- PM/Design: access to roadmap docs, product onboarding session, and first stakeholder mapping.
- Assign onboarding buddy and schedule daily 30m sync for week 1.
Day 8-14 (Context + First deliverable):
- New hire owned tiny deliverable (bug fix, doc, small feature) with PR targeted by day 14.
- Weekly check-in with manager covering blockers, clarity on success milestones.
Day 15-21 (Integration):
- Pair with cross-functional partner, complete first retrospective with sponsor.
- 21-day review: manager, buddy, and new hire confirm next 30/60/90 goals.
Acceptance & paperwork quick flow:
- Offer packet: compensation sheet, equity summary, benefits overview (RTO specifics if needed).
- New hire to sign digital agreements (within 5 business days).
- Recruiter triggers IT access request once signed; people-ops schedules orientation.
Stakeholder responsibilities (one-liners):
- Hiring manager: define outcomes, make final call, own 21-day onboarding plan.
- Recruiter: run sprint schedule, candidate comms, offer logistics.
- Interviewers: timely notes, attend calibration slots, complete feedback in 24h.
- People Ops: enforce compliance, prepare orientation materials, track ramp metrics.
Escalation & risk handling:
- If candidate pipeline < 4 by Day 7, extend sprint or convert to continuous hire (notify people-ops).
- If compensation is a blocker, escalate to compensation panel within 24h.
Metrics to track per sprint (minimal set):
- Time-to-offer (days), Offer-accept rate (%), Candidate NPS (post-process survey), 21-day new hire checklist completion (%), Interviewer feedback completion rate within 24h (%).
After-action (post-sprint retro):
- 30-minute retro with hiring manager + recruiter + 2 interviewers focusing on: pipeline quality, rubric alignment, and onboarding signal adjustments.
- Update role scorecard if multiple candidates reveal a mis-specified skill need.
Templates appended (short snippets):
- Interviewer calibration agenda: 1) 5m purpose, 2) 20m discuss borderline candidates, 3) 5m confirm next steps.
- New hire 21-day review script: 5 prompts for manager (confidence level, blockers, early wins, mentorship needs, next milestones).
Open questions / Next experiments:
- Try a 'two-block interviewing day' vs distributed days and measure interviewer burnout.
- Pilot a candidate micro-survey after first screen to surface early fit signals.
Notes to self:
- Keep the rubric intentionally short to reduce score fatigue.
- Measure and share results publicly each month to get org buy-in.
